imagePrompt: Create one landscape 1536 x 1024 production sprite atlas: exactly TWO columns and THREE rows, six wide cinematic full-scene panels in row-major order 0,1 / 2,3 / 4,5. Each cell fills approximately 768 x 341 pixels (last row 342), flush edge to edge, no gutters or borders. Every cell is a standalone wide composition, not a square image pasted on a wide matte. Painterly literary motion-comic art: watercolor pigment, restrained ink contours, colored-pencil texture, natural anatomy, coherent perspective, grounded feet, credible hands, soft practical light. Keep faces and essential hand/object contact comfortably inside the cell. Show seated bodies joined naturally to chair and table; include chair seats, knees, ankles and shoes when visible. No detached limbs, paper-doll joints, rigid mannequin poses, extra fingers or floating props. Keep cast, clothing, anatomy, furniture and setting consistent across relevant cells. These are fictional adaptation illustrations, not portraits or photographs of real source subjects. NO lettering, labels, logos, readable writing, panel numbers, captions, speech text or watermarks anywhere. Chapter: The Witness. Cast/design continuity: A fictional woman reporter with wavy dark hair tied back, slate-blue jacket and practical trousers, carrying a plain notebook and pencil. Muted street seen through an ordinary doorway, then a modest interior. No recognizable country, uniform, real person, flag, weapon or identifiable captor.. CELL 0: Wide interior edge looking toward a distant ordinary street through an open door. The woman reporter stands in profile, notebook supported in one hand and pencil contacting its page with the other. The notebook and doorway quietly echo a viewfinder; no specific violence is visible in the street. CELL 1: Same viewpoint. The broad edge of the door enters the open street view, beginning to narrow it. The reporter pauses her pencil and lifts her gaze. No hand on the door, captor, struggle or cause of closure is shown. Her body remains naturally balanced. CELL 2: The door leaves a narrow vertical view of the street. The reporter reaches one open hand toward the remaining opening while holding the notebook against her torso with the other. The reaching gesture is cautious and ordinary, with no forced confrontation or physical restraint. CELL 3: Wide small interior. The reporter is now visibly within the room and the doorway is almost shut. She lowers her reaching hand and looks at the notebook held close to her, shoulders tightened. The room boundary now surrounds her; there are no invented bars, chains or detention props. CELL 4: Same room, seated woman and grounded chair fully coherent. The notebook lies open across her lap, one hand supporting its edge, pencil hovering above an unfinished faint mark. Her face registers recognition without theatrical terror. No readable writing and no completed conclusion. CELL 5: Wide quiet interior held on the reporter, open notebook and a little doorway light. Her pencil remains suspended, eyes turned toward the edge of the page. Leave generous empty space beside her and preserve uncertainty; no escape, release, rescue or final fate is added. Editorial limit: Preliminary dramatic concept, not verified incident footage. Do not invent captor identity, detention details, violence, rescue or outcome.
